subject: A date column kind across schemas, kind inference and JSON Lines
brief:
Give tabula a date column kind that works across schemas, kind inference and JSON Lines.

1. `Schema` accepts the kind `date`. A value of such a column is read with `dates.parse_date`: an ISO date gives a date, an ISO date with a time gives a naive datetime (surrounding spaces are allowed, as parse_date allows them), and a value with no text at all is None as for every kind. Edge case: a well-formed but impossible day, such as the thirtieth of February, is not a date; like any value that cannot be read, it raises CoercionError with kind `date` and the offending text.
2. Kind inference only looks for dates when asked: `infer_kind` and `infer_schema` take a keyword `dates` (default False). Without it nothing changes, so a column of ISO dates is still inferred as text. With it, the date kind is tried after float and before str, so text that fits a narrower kind keeps that kind (digits only, even when they look like a compact date, stay int). A column may mix dates and datetimes. The threshold works as for the other kinds, and an impossible day does not fit the date kind. `kind_report` keeps exactly its current keys and counts.
3. `to_jsonl` writes date values as ISO text (year-month-day) and datetime values as ISO text with a T between date and time and whole seconds; any fraction of a second is dropped, so that `parse_date` can read the text back.
4. `from_jsonl` takes a keyword `dates`: column names whose text values are read back with `parse_date`. A missing key or JSON null stays None, and so does a blank string. A value of such a column that is not text (for example a number), or that parse_date rejects, raises CoercionError with that column and kind `date`. A name that is not a column of the result raises KeyError. Without the keyword the values stay text as before, so writing a table with dates and reading it back with its date columns named gives an equal table.

All behavior that the existing tests check must keep working.
